attributes.probed_form: THREE CURES THE ITEMS NAMED WERE REFUTED BY THEIR OWN CALIBRATION AND NOT SHIPPED. (1) Item 4 asked for `--arbitrate` to compare against the BUILT OBJECT. Reproduced verbatim -- `nothing to arbitrate: the working tree IS the banked rolling snapshot, so both halves would measure the same bytes. Edit first, or use --fuzzy for a single-state readout.` exit 1 -- and in that state the snapshot was byte-identical to the tree at 48402 bytes, so both halves compile to the SAME object and proceeding would spend two builds printing two identical rows. What was missing was that the SESSION BASELINE (48333 bytes) and HEAD both DIFFERED and the refusal named neither. Shipped instead: the refusal became a router listing all three candidate states with the flag for each, plus a new `--vs-head`, verified running (`BANKED (HEAD) real 0 fuzzy 100.0000%`). (2) Item 3 implied an object-level extab comparison; measured image-wide, ZERO objects on either side carry an extab-family section, and `datadiff --sections` had been probing for `extab`/`extabindex` spelled without the leading dot that `objdump -h` always produces -- dead twice over. Shipped instead: the readout comes from report.json, and the dead probe keys were removed rather than respelled. (3) Item 6 asked for `laws --residual` per roster row; on the cited signature it returns 15 laws and the closing law is not among them, while a mnemonic query ranks that law first of 40. Shipped instead: the mnemonic join. ONE MORE REVERSAL, inside item 1: the CV sweep's `<=8 byte` cap was first implemented by passing 8 as `fndiff.datum_key`'s own cap, which TRUNCATES every string to 8 bytes and readmits the whole section-alias false-positive class -- 25 findings from 68 set differences against the recorded 7 from 56. Keying at the full DATUM_PREFIX_BYTES and filtering on the resulting length gives 12 findings from 55, and the extra 13 rows in the truncating form were all strings.
attributes.residual: THREE THINGS THIS LANE FOUND AND DID NOT FIX, each belonging to another owner. (a) The scalar-datum sweep's three real-0 rows -- pb_tree::pbTraverseDrawObjects and pb_tree::pbTreeTraverse each reference a target-only 8-byte datum (0xBF80000000000000) that our stream never references, and sfx::SuicideExplosion references an ours-only f32 0.0 the target does not: a wrong constant inside a byte-identical function is precisely the class no other arbiter sees, and each needs the retail split listing read before anything is edited. (b) tools/gdl/pdb20_dump.py carries three E305 rows and is one of the two modules that do work at import; it is script-shaped and was left alone deliberately. (c) `nearmiss --residuals` costs a full pass over every paired object to compute the pool column and now takes appreciably longer than before; nothing measured it as a problem, but a lane running it in a loop should know.

held_fixed: Every item's fix was landed in its own commit with the two suites and the ninja gate run between items, so no two items' calibrations could be confounded. Across all nine, the retail DOL and the project's scores were held constant BY CONSTRUCTION: the lane edited only tools/gdl, memory_graph and AGENTS.md, and touched no src/ file except one temporary reproduction edit to game/anim/atree.c which was measured and then fully restored (`git status --short` shows only the untracked LANE_LOCK).

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run the sweep at a later HEAD and find its real-0 rows dominated by a class the prefix filter does not remove, i.e. that the 12-from-55 survival rate is specific to this tree rather than to the filter. If the three real-0 rows above turn out to be dtk granularity rather than defects, the standing-gate idea is dead before any code is written.
hypothesis.count_consequence: none -- the sweep is a measurement and writes no source; both of the fixes its predecessor produced were count-neutral and byte-identical.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- this lane did not read the retail split listing for any of the three real-0 rows, and says so rather than implying the rows are confirmed defects. The sweep's OWN behaviour was screened against its record's numbers (55 vs 56 set differences, 43 vs 49 prefix-cancelled) at a HEAD six commits later than the record's.
hypothesis.statement: The promoted scalar-datum sweep should become a STANDING gate rather than a tool a lane remembers to run: its whole value is that it sees a wrong constant inside a byte-identical function, and both of run 49's real defects were invisible to every other arbiter. The cheapest form is a row in `defake_gate check` -- it already parses both objects for the unit -- reporting any scalar datum one side references and the other does not, advisory rather than blocking, with the three real-0 rows above as the positive control set.
